feedback: Approved to race. The candidate is valid and is a single-variable test against iteration 9, the best raced design (704.85). Geometry stays at x ±0.03 m at y 0.06 with the 16 mm footprint, mass 0.6, and the same wheels. The controller stays at base_speed 1.1, kp 2.6, ki 0.05, kd 0.9, and sensor_weights [-2,-1,0,1,2]. Only line_loss changes, from last_direction to search_right. Iterations 3 to 9 show that the slalom max_error has stayed between 0.0618 and 0.0661 under every kp, kd, ki, x-coverage and speed setting tried. Slalom line_loss_events have stayed between about 1.0 and 1.45 throughout. The line-loss response is therefore the untested lever, and this race isolates it. The oval and s-bend have rare line losses (0.5 and 0.15 per run in iteration 9), so the score base is unlikely to move much. The main risk is that a fixed left sweep worsens s-bend or oval recovery. Read the result by track. If the oval or s-bend finish rate falls below 0.95, or s-bend completion_time exceeds about 2.8 s, return line_loss to last_direction and keep the other values. If the slalom still goes off track with max_error at or above 0.06 and line_loss_events stay near 1.0 or higher, test search_left next with everything else unchanged. If any slalom run finishes, hold all values and confirm the score rather than change gains.
requested_changes: If the oval or s-bend finish rate drops below 0.95, or s-bend completion_time exceeds about 2.8 s, set line_loss back to last_direction. Iteration 9 reference: oval 20/20 (mean 1.87 s), s-bend 20/20 (mean 2.25 s), with 0.5 and 0.15 line-loss events per run.

If the slalom still ends off track with max_error at or above 0.06 and line_loss_events remain near 1.0 or higher, test line_loss search_left with everything else unchanged. Iterations 3 to 9 keep the slalom max_error between 0.0618 and 0.0661, so a different fixed sweep direction is the next structural test.
If any slalom run finishes under search_right, hold all values and use the next race to confirm the score, rather than changing gains or geometry.
